ConocoPhillips rose 1.64% today, climbing back toward its late-August highs as oil prices ticked up on geopolitical tension. Iran launched attacks on U.S. bases in Jordan over the weekend, prompting Trump to threaten a strong response—a dynamic that typically supports crude prices by raising supply concerns. US oil is trading at $83.90 per barrel today, up from the lows seen mid-week, which directly benefits an integrated oil producer like COP that profits when crude strengthens.

The stock's broader two-week gain of 3.86% reflects a recovery from late-week weakness and sits within the context of shifting Middle East risk and new supply deals—including Trump's Venezuela oil concession announcement. While those Venezuelan reserves are massive on paper, they take years to develop, so near-term oil prices remain the main driver of COP's near-term movement.
